title: Temporal alert suppression & on-call feedback loop for region-aware circuit-fusing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Pager noise spikes during transient multi-region flaps and model rollout churn are causing on-call fatigue. Current alerts fire on raw error rates and tail latency per region and often duplicate across related circuits, resulting in noisy pages and slow human triage.

Goal: Implement a temporal suppression framework combined with region-aware probabilistic fusing and an explicit on-call feedback loop so that: 1) only high-confidence, customer-impacting incidents page humans; 2) automated remediation (circuit open / degraded routing / load-shed) is applied quickly; 3) on-call feedback updates thresholds and suppression windows iteratively.

Proposed approach summary:
- Introduce a short-term suppression window ("temporal fuse") at the alerting layer that groups correlated signals across routes and regions before paging. The fuse uses a configurable burn-rate heuristic (error-budget velocity + cross-region correlation) rather than raw single-metric thresholds.
- Implement region-aware probabilistic fusing: when a region shows transient noise but global SLOs are intact, alerts from that region are deprioritized and only escalate after an amplified burn-rate or cross-region propagation.
- Add a lightweight circuit-fuse controller in the serving runtime that supports soft-open behavior: after N failures in a rolling window trigger, the controller moves a route to soft-open where a small percent (e.g., 10%) of traffic is allowed through as a canary while the rest is routed to a degraded model variant or cached response. Full open happens only on sustained high burn-rate.
- Integrate automation: on high burn-rate + circuit open, orchestrate automated mitigation steps (route-specific load-shedding, model downgrade to quantized variant, or promote cached responses) and create a draft incident with prefilled diagnostics in the Console.
- Build an on-call feedback loop: after an incident or suppression action, the on-call engineer can annotate why a page was noisy (false positive / expected degradation / customer-impacting). The annotation feeds a small ML classifier that suggests future suppression adjustments and adds suggested label changes to alert rules for review.

Why this differs from current work: This ticket focuses on combining temporal grouping, probabilistic fusing, and a runtime-aware soft-open circuit pattern with explicit human feedback rather than only tuning thresholds or runbook text. It is intended to reduce transient pages while preserving rapid response to real SLO breaches.
runbook_outline: 1) Initial detection: observe burn-rate > 5x within a 5m window OR 95th token latency spike > 2s sustained for 2m
2) Temporal fuse: group signals across routes/regions for 60s to suppress duplicates
3) Soft-open circuit: if route-level failures >= 5 within 30s trigger soft-open (10% pass-through) for 2m
4) Automated mitigation during soft-open: route 90% traffic to degraded_model_v1 or cached_response, reduce batch size for bursts
5) Create incident draft in Console with diagnostics (span traces, kv-cache hit-rate, per-region latencies), and page only if group burn-rate persists beyond 3m or customer-impact flag set
6) On-call annotation step: require engineer to mark page as true/false positive and add short reason; if false positive, suppression window increases by 50% for that rule (configurable)
7) Post-incident analysis: automated report generated and suggestions queued for threshold tuning or alert rule changes
automation_playbooks: Trigger: route burn-rate > 10 and global error budget remaining < 30% -> Actions: open soft-circuit, route fallback, post message to #oncall and create incident draft with links to graphs
Trigger: cross-region correlated latency spike (same model route across 2+ regions) -> Actions: start canary rollout freeze, reduce autoscale burst, and increase suppression to avoid duplicate pages

Trigger: persistent circuit-open > 5m -> Actions: escalate to SRE owner, snapshot model state, unpin deployment and rollback to previous stable variant (automated with manual approve), notify customers_if_high_impact
acceptance_criteria: New fuse-based alerting rules deployed for top 30 customer-facing routes
Pager rate for these routes drops >= 40% in the first 2 weeks post-launch while mean time to resolve for real incidents remains <= current baseline
Soft-open circuit implemented in runtime with configurable pass-through percentage and verified via chaos test (inject 10% failure rate)
On-call feedback UI implemented in Console and connected to suggestion pipeline (initial model with precision >= 0.6 on test set)
Automated incident draft creation with prefilled diagnostics verified in staging and security reviewed
